references.text: God calls Abram to leave his father's house and his homeland - this is the event Abraham refers to in 24:7 with the words 'who took me from my father's house and from my homeland'.
God promises Abraham: 'To your offspring I will give this land' - exactly the same wording that Abraham quotes in 24:7 ('לזרעך אתן את הארץ הזאת').
God renews His promise to Abraham concerning the land and countless descendants, strengthening the promise that Abraham refers to in 24:7.
God makes a covenant with Abraham and promises him the land from the river of Egypt to the Euphrates, a formal confirmation of the land promise referred to in 24:7.
God swears by Himself to Abraham and confirms the promise of blessing and descendants. This oath is what Abraham refers to in 24:7 with the words 'who swore to me'.
Abraham repeats the promise that the Lord will send His angel ahead of the servant, parallel to the statement in 24:7 that 'He will send His angel before you'.
Abraham went out in faith to the land he was to inherit and lived as a stranger in the promised land - a consequence of the call and promise referred to in 24:7.
God promises to send His angel ahead of the people to lead them, parallel to Abraham's trust in 24:7 that God 'will send His angel before you'.
Theological parallel: God's promise to give the land to the fathers' offspring as a basis for action.
Theological parallel: The angel as God's instrument to guide them to the promised land.
Theological parallel: The land is given by God and is to be taken possession of as part of His plan.
Theological parallel: The land is God's gift to Abraham's offspring, given as a promise.
Theological parallel: Confession that the land was given as a fulfillment of God's oath to the fathers.
Direct parallel in the same story: The servant's confession of God's guidance in finding a wife.
